Nobody reviews your prose — only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/weed.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) the worst case, a fifty-file staged diff carrying a twenty mebibyte file, is judged by the release binary in under one second on this machine as a median of five, so that the two-second budget holds on a GitHub-hosted runner with room to spare; a file past the size G2 calls unreadable costs one pass over its bytes and no more, and nothing a rule catches in such a file today is lost · evidence expected at: tests/speed.rs

## Definition of done — verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/weed.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload cbdfb83dcfb5 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 map shaped from the umbrella's fit loop and the build brief (revised 2026-09-05), before any code, as the garden law requires; the umbrella map holds fit (F1 to F6), this map holds modules
- 2026-09-05 weed lives in its own repository, not the tilth Cargo workspace: cape-town's correction over the channel and the brief's revision agree; `building-the-garden.md` §5 and §8 still say "in the tilth workspace" and are reported stale to the umbrella rather than followed
- 2026-09-05 process requirement from the owner: build with tend2 loops, pleach conducting, umbel driving, and record every experience with those tools in `docs/dogfood.md`. The brief's "no subagents" line yields to that: workers are pleach nodes, this map is their work order, and the conductor audits the result against the diff
- 2026-09-05 `tilth-core` does not exist; the extraction is conducted first as its own pleach plan against a worktree of tilth (`plans/tilth-core.plan.json`), then this map's plan is emitted. Until the branch is pushed, `.cargo/config.toml` patches the git dependency to the local worktree, the one machine-specific line in the repo, flagged above
- 2026-09-05 `--strict` defined, since the brief uses it without saying what it does: suppressions are reported but not honoured, and a rule that cannot evaluate a file makes the run fail closed (exit 3) instead of skipping the file. A gate an agent can talk out of a block with an allowance it wrote itself is not a gate
- 2026-09-05 fixtures are directory pairs (`before/` committed, `after/` as the working tree), not patch files, so a fixture reads as code in its language and the test replays it through the real git path
- 2026-09-05 the check rules are split across three sequential loops (block, tests, prod) rather than parallel siblings: they share the rule registry file and parallel edits there would merge-conflict on every join; guard, hooks and scan run in parallel with rules-tests since they own disjoint files
- 2026-09-05 calibration repos follow the fit loop (tilth, pleach, tend2, copeca, umbel) rather than the brief's list with rctrl; several have fewer than 200 commits on their default branch, so the run takes every commit available and reports the count
- 2026-09-05 scope-out: no rules that name vendors or products; no inbound injection quarantine; no spend rules (settled on the umbrella loop, not re-argued here)
- 2026-09-05 `--strict` accepted by the umbrella with one refinement recorded in the brief: strict never escalates warn-level results to block; severity is the rule's, not the flag's
- 2026-09-05 with core, sarif and check-face landed and the reader seam waiting on almaty, guard, hooks and garden-fit were re-pointed to run on G1 rather than wait for rules-block; the rule loops and scan still wait for the seam
- 2026-09-05 milestone 1 met by almaty: tilth-core exists on `garden/tilth-core` at 7f38db5, pushed, so weed pins a rev and carries no machine-specific line; the push the owner was asked for is done by the tilth agent's PR
- 2026-09-05 cape-town added six binding checks on the umbrella loop (determinism, recall by mutation injection, never panic, a latency budget, independent classification, suppression-rate tracking); they landed here as the hardening, recall and calibration-audit loops, a suppression-rate check on calibration, the latency budget above, and a CI clause on garden-fit
- 2026-09-05 the owner settled all three reserved decisions through cape-town on the channel: the name weed, the accent bramble `#8E3B5E`, the licence MIT. The human check is approved on that word; the only owner-only actions left are on GitHub (publish, Pages), and the owner asked for the branch to be pushed and a draft pull request opened, which is done (#1)
- 2026-09-06 built by pleach node `weed` (claude/opus, codex audit), all three code checks stamped, landed through `pleach land`. The matrix runs 200 cells, each under a `weed.toml` that leaves one rule on, and asserts set equality: the fire cell reports its rule and nothing else, the silent cell nothing; every cell came back right the first time. The self-check found 36 block-level findings on weed's own tree and every one was weed being right: 34 were the adversarial fixtures, so `[scope] specimens` is now on in weed's own `weed.toml`; one was a work marker in the first line of `r3.rs`, reworded; one was `weed.toml` arriving from the root commit, allowed with its reason and bounded by a test that an ordinary edit still blocks. The latency budget found the real bug: a fifty-file diff with a twenty mebibyte file took 86 seconds with every rule off, because the face outlined every side of every file before a rule asked; weed stops reading a file as code at the mebibyte G2 already calls unreadable, still reads its lines, and the worst case answers in 1.2 seconds. Calibration and recall were measured before that cap; the corpus is pinned, so the next run settles whether a figure moves. The worker's notes are in docs/dogfood/weed.md
- 2026-09-06 CI failed the latency budget on a GitHub-hosted runner: the worst case measured 2131 ms against 2000, while the same release binary passed in the other job on another runner. It is 1.2 s on the owner's machine, which is the edge of the budget once a shared runner's slowness is added, and the budget tests had been timing the release binary in both jobs. The budget is the spec and is not widened: the tests now run on the release profile only, and the check above asks for the headroom the claim needs by making the worst case itself cheaper

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file — check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green — it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Scratch (probes, experiments, packets, session logs) goes under `$TMPDIR`, written through the shell only, never with the Write or Edit tool, and never under `.loop-scratch/` or anywhere in this worktree: the collector stages every path the editor touched, a path outside the worktree kills the delivery, and the hygiene gate judges whatever is left in the tree, including its secret scan.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root — what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
